title: epan: Restore curr_proto_layer_num after every dissector
description:
The current implementation restores the "current protocol layer number"
(for the current protocol, not the total number of layers) only when
a subdissector did not add anything to the tree, and restores it to the
last added layer. This only works under a model where a protocol does
not add additional fields after control returns to it from other
dissectors it calls. In cases where a protocol has multiple PDUs or
records, or simply calls helper subdissectors several times, the
pinfo->curr_proto_layer_num can refer to the other dissectors that
processed bytes.

This affects, among other things, how filters that use the layer
operator match.

This can be observed with some of the sample files. E.g., in
"quic-fragmented-handshakes.pcapng.gz" where the QUIC dissector
calls the TLS dissector several times due to fragmentation,
even though there is only one QUIC layer, frame 19 matches
"quic.padding_length#2 == 103" instead of
"quic.padding_length#1 == 103", because that field appears
after the second TLS layer added.

Similarly, in "tls-over-tls.pcapng.gz" frame 5 the Client Key
Exchange handshake record fields match on layer 5 instead of layer
1, because the record follows a Certificate handshake record that
calls the x509ce dissector five times.
"tls.handshake.type#5 == 16" matches instead of
"tls.handshake.type#1 == 16"

Restore the current protocol layer number after returning from a
subdissector at the same time as restoring the current protocol
name.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -561,12 +561,9 @@ class TestDfilterValueString:
         dfilter = 'vals(tls.handshake.type) contains "Client"'
         checkDFilterCount(dfilter, 2)
 
-    # A Client Hello appears in tls layer 1 in one packet...
-    # In the other packet, it's the second TLS PDU, but the TLS
-    # dissector is only called once - but it gets called layer 5
-    # because that's the layer of the last successfully called
-    # dissector, as x509ce gets called 5 times by the previous
-    # Handshake PDU. This seems like a bug.
+    # A Client Hello appears in TLS layer 1 in one packet, and
+    # Client Key Exchange appears in TLS layer 1 in another (as
+    # the second record at that layer).
     def test_value_string_func_layer(self, checkDFilterCount):
         dfilter = 'vals(tls.handshake.type#1) contains "Client"'
-        checkDFilterCount(dfilter, 1)
+        checkDFilterCount(dfilter, 2)
